answer: A proposed bridge audit plants blind, precommitted canaries in each seat’s dune queue; validators open the correct verdict after signed grades and burn a bond for a wrong grade. Nectar pays only seats locking N units each while N seats are active, with coin nullifiers barring reuse. A farm can share a model and borrow coins, but k new seats lock at least k² distinct units for 30 epochs; a correlated canary miss burns every faulty bond. Lenders still finance all locked units, and skipping a bond yields no seat. Validators would enforce this, not MinePoA today.
